practice.intro: Some days are harder than others. What you do next is yours.

items.question: You studied for a test and still failed it. What's the best next step?

choices.text: Decide studying doesn't work for you.
Hide the test and hope nobody asks.
Promise yourself you'll study twice as long next time.
Look at which questions you missed and figure out why.

hints: Which one tells you what actually went wrong?
Is more time the fix if you don't know the problem?
items.reasoning: A bad grade is information. Use it before you judge yourself. That's Be Responsible.

distractors.A: One test doesn't prove that. It tells you something to fix.
distractors.B: Hiding it doesn't change it, and it skips the part that helps.
distractors.C: More of the same studying might give you more of the same result.

items.question: You were out sick for a week, and the work has piled up. What do you do first?

choices.text: Make a list and ask your teacher what matters most.
Try to do all of it tonight.
Skip the old stuff and just keep up with the new.
Wait until you feel caught up to go back to class.

hints: Who knows which pieces matter most?
Which one turns a mountain into steps?
items.reasoning: A pile gets smaller one piece at a time, starting with the right piece. That's Be Responsible.

distractors.B: One night can't hold a week, and you'll be wiped out tomorrow.
distractors.C: The old stuff is often what the new stuff is built on.
distractors.D: Staying away makes the pile bigger, not smaller.

items.question: You told yourself you'd start studying earlier this time. You didn't, again. What now?

choices.text: Give up on it. You're just not that kind of student.
Wait until next unit to try again.
Start now, even if it's only twenty minutes.
Pull an all-nighter the day before.

hints: When is the next chance to start?
Which choice doesn't need a perfect plan?
items.reasoning: Missing the plan once doesn't cancel the plan. Start where you are. That's Be Responsible.

distractors.A: "That kind of student" is a habit, and habits can change.
distractors.B: Waiting turns one miss into two.
distractors.D: That's the same plan that didn't work last time.

items.question: You lost your starting spot on the team. What's the best response?

choices.text: Quit. They'll be sorry.
Ask the coach what to work on, and work on it.
Complain to your friends about the coach.
Stop trying hard in practice.

hints: Who decides who starts?
Which one gives you a way back?
items.reasoning: Asking what to fix, then fixing it, is how spots get earned back. That's Be Responsible.

distractors.A: Quitting makes sure you never get the spot back.
distractors.C: Complaining changes nothing about the depth chart.
distractors.D: Practice is the only place you can show you're ready.

items.question: Your teacher's comments on your essay sting. What do you do?

choices.text: Throw the paper away.
Decide the teacher doesn't like you.
Read it again later, then ask which one change would help most.
Argue about every comment right then.

hints: What's the comment for?
When can you read it without the sting?
items.reasoning: Feedback is someone taking your work seriously. Hear it out, then use it. That's Be Respectful.

distractors.A: Then the help in it is gone too.
distractors.B: Comments are about the essay, not about you.
distractors.D: Arguing while you're upset usually means you haven't heard it yet.

items.question: Your group's project got a lower grade than you hoped, and everyone is blaming each other. What helps?

choices.text: Look at the rubric together and figure out what to fix next time.
Decide whose fault it was.
Say nothing and never work with them again.
Tell the teacher the grade is unfair.

hints: What would make the next project better?
Which one keeps the group a group?
items.reasoning: Blame looks backward. Fixing it together looks forward. That's Be Respectful.

distractors.B: Even if you're right, it won't raise the next grade.
distractors.C: You'll probably work with them again. Leave the door open.
distractors.D: Start with the rubric. It usually shows where the points went.

items.question: A coach corrects you in front of the whole team. What do you do?

choices.text: Roll your eyes so everyone knows you disagree.
Argue back right there.
Walk away.
Listen, say "okay," and talk to the coach privately later if you need to.

hints: Where is the best place to disagree?
What does listening cost you?
items.reasoning: Taking a correction calmly in front of others shows more strength than fighting it. That's Be Respectful.

distractors.A: Everyone sees it, and it makes the next practice harder.
distractors.B: An argument in front of the team rarely goes your way.
distractors.C: Walking off turns a correction into a bigger problem.

items.question: Someone beat you in a competition, fair and square. What do you do?

choices.text: Say they got lucky.
Shake hands and ask what they did to prepare.
Leave before the results are read.
Say you weren't really trying.

hints: What could you learn from the person who won?
Which one would you want if you had won?
items.reasoning: Respecting a fair win, and learning from it, makes you tougher to beat next time. That's Be Respectful.

distractors.A: If it was fair, it wasn't luck, and saying so costs you.
distractors.C: Leaving says more about the loss than staying would.
distractors.D: Nobody believes it, and it takes away from them.

items.question: You keep making the same mistake, and you're getting down on yourself. What helps most?

choices.text: Call yourself names until you stop doing it.
Talk to yourself the way you'd talk to a friend: "Not yet."
Stop trying that thing.
Pretend it doesn't bother you.

hints: What would you tell a friend in your spot?
Which one keeps you trying?
items.reasoning: Being kind to yourself isn't going easy. It's what keeps you in the game. That's Be Kind.

distractors.A: Harsh words usually make people quit, not improve.
distractors.D: It still bothers you, and now you're handling it alone.

items.question: A friend failed a test and says they're giving up on the class. What do you say?

choices.text: "Yeah, that class is impossible."
Nothing. It's their business.
"Just copy my homework."
"One test isn't the whole class. Want to study together?"

hints: What would help them try again?
Which one is help that actually helps?
items.reasoning: Sometimes kindness is reminding someone the season isn't over. That's Be Kind.

distractors.B: A word from a friend can matter more than you think.
distractors.C: That helps for a night and hurts on the next test.

items.question: You trip in front of everyone in the hallway, and people laugh. What's the best way to handle it?

choices.text: Get angry at whoever laughed loudest.
Skip that hallway for the rest of the year.
Shake it off, maybe laugh too, and keep going.
Replay it in your head all day.

hints: Will anyone remember this next week?
Which one gets you past it fastest?
items.reasoning: Everybody stumbles. Going easy on yourself is the next play. That's Be Kind.

distractors.A: That makes the moment bigger and longer.
distractors.B: One bad moment shouldn't run your whole year.
distractors.D: You'll remember it far longer than anyone else does.

items.question: Your friend didn't make the cast of the school play and has been avoiding everyone. What could you do?

choices.text: Check in, and invite them to something low-key.
Give them space forever.
Tell them it's not a big deal.
Post about how unfair the cast list is.

hints: What tells someone they still belong?
Which one doesn't tell them how to feel?
items.reasoning: Showing up for a friend after a setback helps them get back up. That's Be Kind.

distractors.B: Some space helps. Forever turns into lonely.
distractors.C: It is a big deal to them. Telling them otherwise rarely helps.
distractors.D: That keeps the hurt going, and the cast list is still the cast list.

items.question: Everything is due this week, and you're too stressed to sleep. What's the best step?

choices.text: Stay up all night to get it all done.
Ignore it and hope it goes away.
Write it all down, pick the first thing, and get some sleep.
Drink energy drinks and push through.

hints: What does a tired brain do on a test?
Which one makes the week feel smaller?
items.reasoning: A list and a night's sleep do more than panic does. If it keeps up, talk to an adult. That's Be Safe.

distractors.A: One all-nighter makes the rest of the week harder.
distractors.B: It doesn't go away. It just gets closer.
distractors.D: That trades one problem for a crash later.

items.question: After a tough loss, a teammate wants to go start something with the other team. What do you do?

choices.text: Go along so you look loyal.
Film it in case something happens.
Cheer them on from the side.
Walk away, and help your teammate walk away too.

hints: What happens to the team if it turns into a fight?
Which choice protects everyone?
items.reasoning: Losing hurts. A fight makes it worse for everybody. That's Be Safe.

distractors.A: Loyal means keeping them out of trouble, not following them into it.
distractors.B: Filming keeps it going and can hurt someone further.
distractors.C: Cheering it on makes you part of it.

items.question: After a bad week, you're tempted to game all night to forget about it. What's the better call?

choices.text: Put it down at a normal time. Tomorrow's a fresh start.
Play until you feel better, however long that takes.
Skip school tomorrow to catch up on sleep.
Keep it secret so nobody worries.

hints: How will tomorrow go on two hours of sleep?
Which choice gives you a better tomorrow?
items.reasoning: A reset needs rest. Tomorrow is the comeback. That's Be Safe.

distractors.B: Late nights usually make a bad week longer.
distractors.C: Missing a day adds to the pile you're trying to escape.
distractors.D: If the week was that bad, someone who cares should know.

items.question: You get hurt at practice, but you want to hide it so you don't lose your spot. What do you do?

choices.text: Play through it. Nobody needs to know.
Tell the trainer or coach right away.
Tape it up yourself and keep going.
Wait and see if it gets worse.

hints: What happens to a hidden injury?
Who can actually help it heal?
items.reasoning: Getting hurt is part of playing. Hiding it is how a small injury becomes a season. That's Be Safe.

distractors.A: Playing hurt often turns a short break into a long one.
distractors.C: You might not know how bad it is.
distractors.D: Waiting is how injuries get worse.
